{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-wv-class-e","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"16f77ce182a94547c2de75312b6d63bc952a8b95fa697e1981104d4bfa02bcb0","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-wv-class-e:lineage:24","source_registry_sha256":"2261abaab8e2b1aaff5b8a336e3bfcf845adaa75847f0210442061783d7f9afb","source_liveness_sha256":"9a1fb68777f5e9d5c4b27899084cc233b265410fee506dfe6554447a61ea026e"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Knowledge examination","heading":"C — Knowledge examination","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Knowledge examination

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A01
The driver examination is a series of tests measuring your qualifications against established standards, covering vision, color recognition, knowledge of traffic laws, recognition of road signs, and the ability to operate a motor vehicle safely and skillfully in traffic [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A01
Examiners are trained professionals who ride along only to see that you can control the vehicle and observe the rules of the road, so concentrate on your driving rather than your errors, and a mark on the score sheet does not necessarily mean you made an error [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A01
On behalf of the state the DMV asks every licensed driver to drive as well as or better than during the examination [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A01
Every applicant, new or renewing, must pass the vision screening, which requires twenty-forty vision or better using both eyes, with or without conventional corrective lenses, and no serious visual defect, and depth perception, color recognition and peripheral vision may also be checked [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A01
Special lens arrangements such as bi-optic or telescopic lenses may not be used to satisfy the visual acuity standard [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A01
If glasses or contact lenses are needed to reach twenty-forty vision the license carries a corrective lenses restriction code, and an applicant with only one eye may pass if that eye sees twenty-forty or better [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A01
An applicant with vision below twenty-forty or a serious visual defect fails the screening and is told to consult a vision specialist, and if the vision cannot be corrected to that level a licensed vision care specialist must send the DMV a statement describing the condition and recommending whether and under what restrictions the applicant can drive safely [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A01
Vision specialist statements may be reviewed by the Driver's License Advisory Board at the discretion of the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles before an instruction permit or license is issued [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A01
The knowledge examination has at least twenty-five questions based on the basic knowledge, traffic rules, regulations, signs and markings found in the handbook [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A01
Automated testing is given at all locations, you must answer nineteen of the twenty-five questions correctly to pass, and because the test has a time limit any question not answered in the prescribed time counts as incorrect [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A01
An audio version of the knowledge examination with headphones is available for the reading impaired, it covers the same material under the same rules, DMV employees may not read, reword or explain questions beyond what printed-test applicants receive, and headsets are limited so you may have to wait [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A02
Every first-time applicant for a driver's license must complete a short DUI awareness course given upon passing the road skills test, including out-of-state drivers coming into West Virginia even if previously licensed here, and completion is shown by a card or a stamp on the application [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A02
The vehicle used for the road skills test must comply with registration, vehicle inspection and equipment laws, needs a valid inspection sticker and proof of insurance, and vehicle defects may constitute failure of the examination [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A02
The examiner may permit a minor defect to be corrected so the examination continues, but you may not continue the examination in another vehicle on the same test date [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A02
The examiner cannot give the driving test unless the vehicle is in safe condition and legally equipped, and an applicant who cannot both locate and demonstrate every piece of safety equipment, including the parking or emergency brake, automatically fails the road skills test [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A02
Illegal equipment includes red or blue flashing lights, which only authorized emergency vehicles may carry, sirens, bells or whistles, a cutout or loud-sounding muffler, signs, posters or stickers on the windshield or windows unless required or permitted by law, and more than one spotlight [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A02
It is also illegal to have more than two side cowl or fender lights, more than two backup lights, backup lights that show light while the vehicle moves forward, or any load extending beyond the fender line on the left side or more than six inches beyond the fender line on the right side [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F18 | anchor: A02
Further illegal equipment includes a vehicle without safety glass, windows tinted to less than thirty-five percent light transmission, a broken or cracked windshield, holes in the body, broken lenses, and doors or windows that do not operate [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]
